Subject: CalderaX: deal-level TPS/latency model & capacity hedging proposal

Alex / team —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Attached is the initial capacity model and a short simulation (caldera_usage_profile.csv, capacity_simulation_v1.xlsx) that maps CalderaX's traffic forecast into tokens/sec and GPU slab needs. High-level assumptions we used (please flag if any are off):

- Target p95 latency for inference: 300 ms (customer requirement)
- Model selected for serving: vicuna-13b-8k-quant (production-verified in our catalog)
- Baseline throughput per H100 (quant path, with KV cache warmed and modest batching): ~800 tokens/sec at p95 <= 300ms
- Average prompt + generation length: 450 tokens (includes system + generation)
- Customer projected steady-state RPS: 5 requests/sec (CalderaX projection v1) -> 5 * 450 = 2,250 tokens/sec

Simple math: 2,250 tokens/sec required / 800 tokens/sec per GPU = 2.8 -> ceil to 3 GPUs to meet steady-state SLA.

Headroom and enterprise guardrails: we recommend reserving additional capacity for:
- 40% safety buffer for unexpected spikes and KV cache cold starts
- Reserved slab sizing granularity (we allocate whole GPUs per slab)

Applying a 40% buffer: 3 * 1.4 = 4.2 -> round up to 5 GPUs.

Recommendation (short):
- Dedicated slab recommendation for committed SKU: 6 x H100 (reserved)
  - Rationale: 5 GPUs covers steady-state + 40% headroom; we reserve 1 extra GPU as operational buffer during rollout and initial canary.
  - Expected steady-state p95: <=300ms (with KV cache warm).
  - Burst fallback plan: automatic routing to hosted instances if sustained usage > slab for >10 minutes (we'll describe the fallback in the SLA).

Alternative options (cost trade-offs):
- If CalderaX agrees to enable application-level caching + short-term prefix caching (we estimate 20-30% token reduction), the effective tokens/sec drops to ~1,600–1,800 and required GPUs reduce to 2–3 (plus headroom -> 4 GPUs).
- If you want an aggressive cost-first plan we can do a hybrid: 4 reserved GPUs + dynamic burst on-demand.

Attachments: caldera_usage_profile.csv (CSV), CalderaX_MVP-eval.pdf (PDF), capacity_simulation_v1.xlsx (Excel).

Next steps I propose:
1) Ben / Karthik confirm the baseline per-GPU throughput assumption (I've used our catalog bench for vicuna-13b-quant on H100).
2) Alex confirm RPS and average tokens-per-request (if you have a more detailed usage histogram, send it).
3) We schedule a 45-min sizing review with your infra and SRE to walk the canary and fallback.

I'll loop in the SLA/legal thread once we lock the slab count.

— Rachel

Subject: Re: CalderaX: deal-level TPS/latency model & capacity hedging proposal

Thanks Rachel — good first pass. A couple of quick modeling notes from my side after running the sim sheet through a few scenarios:

1) Batching + adaptive micro-batching: If the client payload distribution supports safe batching (many requests with <500 token inputs arriving in short windows), we can often increase effective per-GPU throughput by ~25–35% without materially impacting p95 for interactive flows. That reduces the required GPUs.

2) KV prefix caching impact: For CalderaX's workload we saw ~18% median token saving in the sample you provided (repeat prefixes). If we combine caching (18%) + conservative batching (20%), combined effective token reduction is ~34% (not additive perfectly but directionally correct). That takes the 2,250 tokens/sec down to ~1,485 tokens/sec.

3) Updated GPU calc (conservative): 1,485 / 800 = 1.86 -> 2 GPUs baseline. Add 40% headroom -> 2.8 -> round to 3 GPUs.

4) Operational recommendation: start the contract with 4 reserved GPUs (gives ~1.3x extra headroom vs the conservative combined-savings model), then scale to 6 if usage patterns show high variance in MTD. The 4-GPU starter reduces customer cost while keeping the canary/resilience targets intact.

I've attached the scenario workbook (capacity_simulation_v1.xlsx) with the two extra tabs I used: batching_sensitivity and cache_effects.

Quick ask to Alex (cc'd): can you confirm the distribution of prompt lengths across 90th/50th percentiles? That will let us pick a conservative tokens/request number for canary sizing.

— Ben

Alex — thanks for the detail. Responding to each of your asks: 

1) Canary plan we are happy to run: 2 reserved H100s + automatic burst routing to Redwood-hosted pool when steady utilization exceeds 70% for >5 minutes. We'll provide a warm-start runbook (recommended synthetic traffic pattern to prime KV cache for ~20 mins) — expectation is KV warm cuts tail by ~150–250ms in the p95 for common prefixes.

2) SLA credit: we can agree to a p95 credit trigger at 350ms for a rolling 3-day window with a remediation playbook. Legal will define the credit terms, but we can include that threshold in the commercial term sheet as a negotiation point.

3) Cold-start constraints: depending on model context length and dataset, full KV warm is best after ~15–30 minutes of representative traffic. For short-lived features we recommend explicit synthetic warmers at deploy. We'll include recommended API warm-up scripts in the runbook.

4) Revised phased commitment document (summary):
- Phase A (Canary, 30 days): 2 reserved H100s (customer pays canary rate) + automatic burst to hosted fleet.
- Phase B (scale-up, next 30–60 days): 4 reserved H100s — monitor utilization and growth.
- Phase C (enterprise commit): 6 reserved H100s for steady-state SLA and headroom.

I'll attach an updated commercial appendix with cost deltas and will loop in Solutions Legal to capture the SLA clause. Meeting: I've scheduled a 45-minute sizing review for Thu 08/20 10:00 AM PT — invite sent separately.

Next steps for Alex: share the 90/50/99 token distribution sample and confirm procurement timeline; we'll push an updated appendix by EOD tomorrow.
